translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "al-Nās." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:

Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind (1) the King of mankind (2) the God of mankind (3) from the evil of the withdrawing whisperer (4) who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5) from among jinn and mankind (6)
He, exalted be His mention, says to His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: Say, Muḥammad: I seek protection
in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind

. He is the King of all creation, their humans, their jinn and others. By this He informed those who revere people, as believers revere their Lord, that He is the King of the one whom they revere. That reverence lies within His kingdom and authority, His power operates upon the one revered, and He is more deserving of reverence and more entitled to be worshipped than any of those people whom they revere and worship.
. He says: the object of worship of the people, to whom worship belongs to the exclusion of everything besides Him.
from the evil of the whisperer
. He means: from the evil of Satan.
) at one time and whispers at another. As has been mentioned, he withdraws only when the servant mentions his Lord.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥakīm b. Jubayr, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: He said: There is no newborn but the whisperer is upon his heart. When he reasons and mentions God, it withdraws, and when he is heedless, it whispers. He said: that is His saying

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from Manṣūr, from Saʿīd [Fn 2], from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he said: Satan crouches on the heart of the son of Ādam. When he forgets and is heedless, he whispers, and when he mentions God, Satan withdraws. [Fn 3]

c: He [Ibn Ḥumayd] said: Mihrān told us, from ʿUthmān, from Mujāhid.
m: . He said: he spreads out; when he mentions God, he withdraws and contracts, and when he is heedless, he spreads out.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both [ʿĪsā and Waraqāʾ] from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: , he said: Satan is on the heart of the human, and when he mentions God, Satan withdraws. [Fn 4]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: . He said: it is Satan, and he is also the withdrawer: when the servant mentions his Lord, he withdraws. He whispers and withdraws. [Fn 5]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: from the evil of the whisperer, the withdrawing one
. He means Satan, who whispers in the breast of the son of Ādam and withdraws when he mentions God.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from his father.
m: He said: It was mentioned to me that Satan, or he said "the whisperer," blows into the heart of a person at times of grief and of joy, and when he mentions God, Satan withdraws. [Fn 1]

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: is the one who whispers at one time and withdraws at another, from among the jinn and humans. It used to be said that the devil of humans is harder on people than the devil of the jinn: the devil of the jinn whispers and you do not see him, whereas this one confronts you face to face. [Fn 2]

x: It has been reported from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ that he used to say about this:
from the evil of the whisperer
is the one who whispers, calling in the breasts of people to obedience to himself, until he is answered in what he called them to of obedience to him. Once he is answered in that, he withdraws.
Mention of the report to this effect:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he said: it is Satan, who commands him, and when he is obeyed, he withdraws. [Fn 3]

x: The correct view on this question, in my opinion, is to say that God, exalted be His mention, commanded His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ to seek refuge in Him from the evil of a devil who whispers at one time and withdraws at another. He did not restrict the whispering to one of its kinds, nor the withdrawing to one manner to the exclusion of another. The devil may whisper by calling to disobedience of God, and when he is obeyed in it, he withdraws. He may also whisper by forbidding obedience to God, and when the servant remembers the command of his Lord, obeys Him in it and disobeys Satan, he withdraws. So in both of his states he is a whisperer and a withdrawer, and this attribute is his.
who whispers in the breasts of mankind
. By this He means Satan the whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of people, both their jinn and their humans.
who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5) from among jinn and mankind
?" the answer is that God has named them
in this place, as He named them elsewhere "men" (
And that there were men of mankind who sought refuge with men of the jinn
[al-Jinn 72:6]. So He called the jinn "men," and in the same way He made some of them
. It has been related of one of the Arabs that he said, while narrating: "A group of the jinn came and stood, and it was said: Who are you? They said:
of the jinn." He made some of them
, and the same applies to what is in the revelation.

notes.en: Al-Hafiz cited it in al-Taghliq (4/381) from the author. Abd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/410); through him al-Hakim (2/541), and through al-Hakim al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (676), also transmitted it. In Tafsir Mujahid (p. 762), it is transmitted through al-Thawri with this chain. Al-Diya transmitted it in al-Mukhtara (172) through al-Aʿmash, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/420) to Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره الحافظ في التغليق 4/ 381 عن المصنف، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 410 - ومن طريقه الحاكم 2/ 541، وعنه البيهقى في الشعب (676) - وفى تفسير مجاهد ص 762 من طريق الثورى به، وأخرجه الضياء في المختارة (172) من طريق الأعمش، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 420 إلى ابن أبي الدنيا وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Sufyan.” The adopted reading follows the sources that document the report; see Tahdhib al-Kamal (28/546).
notes.ar: في النسخ: (سفيان). والمثبت من مصادر التخريج، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 28/ 546.

notes.en: Al-Hafiz transmitted it in al-Taghliq (4/381) through Ibn Humayd with this chain. Ibn Abi Shaybah (13/369) and al-Diya in al-Mukhtara (393) transmitted it through Jarir. Al-Diya’s version reads “from Mansur and a man.” Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/420) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الحافظ في التغليق 4/ 381 من طريق ابن حميد به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 369، والضياء في المختارة (393) من طريق جرير به، وعند الضياء: عن منصور ورجل، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 420 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Abd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/410) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 410 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir (8/559) from al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, as his statement.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 559 عن المعتمر بن سليمان، عن أبيه قوله.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/420) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 420 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir (8/509) from al-ʿAwfi, from Ibn ʿAbbas.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 509 عن العوفي، عن ابن عباس.
